---
title: "check-macro-expansions.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags math which writes out by hand
what a shared macro already says.
It is [gha#1218](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1218),
the check behind the rule in psw's
[concise expressions](https://morrison-lab.github.io/psw/chapters/notation/concise-expressions.html)
page.
Two cases motivated it:
the left side of the bias--variance decomposition written as
`\E{\paren{\newoutvar - \predvalf{\newpredval}}^2}`
where `\E{\sqf{\prederrf{\predvalf{\newpredval}}}}` names the same prediction error
([mlg#193](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/mlg/pull/193)),
and a hand-built squared bias where `\sqf{\biassymf{...}}` exists
([mlg#192](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/mlg/pull/192)).

## What it flags

The check reads the macros file (`macros-file`,
default `latex-macros/macros.qmd`) and builds a table of expansions
from every single-line `\providecommand`, `\newcommand`, `\renewcommand` or `\def`
whose body is structured enough to recognise.
Inside `$...$` and `$$...$$` math on a line a pull request adds,
in `.qmd`, `.Rmd` and `.md` files,
text that matches a macro's expansion is reported with the macro that names it.
For example, `\sum_{i=1}^n` is reported as `\sumin`,
and `\tp{X} W X` as `\qform`.

- A `#1`, `#2`, ... in a body is a wildcard for a macro, a letter or a number,
  with an optional subscript.
  A `#1` that appears twice must match the same text both times,
  so `\tp{X} W Z` is not a quadratic form.
- Whitespace and braces between tokens do not matter,
  so `\sum_{ i = 1 }^{ n }` matches too.
- Several macros with one expansion are reported together
  (`\sumin or \sumto`).
  When matches overlap, the longest one is reported.
- A body is *structured enough* when it has at least four tokens
  (commands, symbols, words and placeholders, not braces) and is not an alias of other macros.
  A lone font wrapper such as `\mathcal{H}` or `\operatorname{rank}` has two tokens and is never flagged,
  because the same glyphs are often a different concept.
  `\begin{aligned}` is likewise not flagged.

## What it does not flag

- a line that already uses the macro (for that macro);
- the line that defines a macro;
- text outside math;
- a code fence or code span, an HTML comment, or YAML front matter;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-macro-expansions: allow -->`,
  the opt-out for a derivation that rewrites the chunk on purpose;
- a macro named in `exclude`.
  The default excludes `hist`,
  whose body `\bar{#1}_{#2}` is also how a plain sample mean is written,
  so the table cannot tell the two apart.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so existing hits are not reflagged on every unrelated edit.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose,
for example to count the hits a repository still carries
before turning `fail` on.

Every run prints how many lines, files and expansions it examined.

## Limitations

- An expression split across lines is not found.
- The table cannot tell whether a hit is the concept the macro names.
  `\bar{x}_1` may be a sample mean or a treatment history.
  Mark a deliberate case with the `allow` comment, or list the macro in `exclude`.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.

## Inputs

| Input            | Type    | Default | Description |
| ---------------- | ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `macros-file`    | string  | `'latex-macros/macros.qmd'` | Path of the macros file whose single-line macro definitions give the expansions. A missing file skips the check with a warning. |
| `exclude`        | string  | `'hist'` | Comma- or newline-separated macro names (no backslash) never flagged. |
| `globs`          | string  | `'*.qmd *.Rmd *.md'` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore`   | string  | `''`    | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `submodules`     | string  | `'true'` | Passed to `actions/checkout`, so the `latex-macros` submodule is available. |
| `submodule-paths` | string  | `''`     | Whitespace-separated submodule paths to initialize instead of `submodules`, for a repository with a private submodule beside the public one this check needs. |
| `fail`           | boolean | `false` | Fail the workflow when math spells out a macro's expansion. Warn-only by default. |
| `whole-tree`     | boolean | `false` | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string  | `'3.x'` | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | `'ubuntu-latest'` | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-macro-expansions.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags math on lines a PR adds that writes out by hand what a shared macro
# already says (such as `\sum_{i=1}^n` where `\sumin` exists in the latex-macros submodule's macros.qmd).
# Warn-only by default. Skips with a warning when the macros file is missing.
# Mark a derivation step that rewrites the chunk on purpose with `<!-- check-macro-expansions: allow -->`.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check math that spells out a macro expansion

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-macro-expansions.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   macros-file: 'latex-macros/macros.qmd'  # where the macros are defined
    #   exclude: 'hist'                         # macro names (no backslash) never flagged
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md'                     # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'    # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                              # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                        # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
    #   runs-on: private-runner                # self-hosted runner label (private repositories only)
```

See
[`examples/check-macro-expansions.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-macro-expansions.yml)
for the full caller stub.
